question: Can a permissionless caller of nuke(tokenId) extract more than the designed cap (<=50%/call), bypass the ownership/approval/maturity guards, re-nuke a burned token, or drive the fund accounting to underflow/insolvency?
answer: No. All three guards (ownership, NukeFund-approval, maturity) revert unauthorized calls; the claim is exactly the capped (fund/2) or proportional (fund*factor/MAX_DENOMINATOR) amount and never exceeds fund/2 (no underflow); a burned token cannot be re-nuked; multiple nukes stay bounded and solvent.

cases.evidence: 3 reverts with the contract's own messages

cases.scenario: high factor -> claim capped at fund/2

cases.note: each call <=50% of current fund; 25% remains
